This process typically involves a 3-way classification decision: Entailment, Contradiction, and Neutral. The system for monotonicity reasoning operates by first tagging tokens in the premise text with polarity annotations, such as \(\uparrow\) and \(\downarrow\), which are fundamental to the logic. These annotations are linked to natural logic inference rules that guide the generation of entailments and contradictions through span replacements. For instance, in the sentence "All schoolgirls are on the train," the token "schoolgirls" is annotated with \(\downarrow\), indicating that it can be replaced with a more specific concept to create an entailment.
